Jordan: Quick sync — I'm digging into the p99 spikes from last night. Where's the one-stop place for traces + token throughput so I can correlate TTFT vs tokens/sec? Need to file a tiny alert tweak if we can confirm it's noise.

Priya: Grafana -> Observability > Latency Overview is the start. Panels to check: 
- "Latency: time-to-first-token (per-route)"
- "Throughput: tokens/sec by instance"
- "p50/p95/p99 histogram heatmap"
Links: https://grafana.redwoodinfra.com/d/latency/overview and the quick query explorer: https://grafana.redwoodinfra.com/explore
Also check Jaeger traces from the trace id in the panel — pattern: https://jaeger.redwoodinfra.com/trace/<trace_id> :eyes:

Mike: For quick local queries, use these PromQL snippets in Explore: 
```
# p95 request latency (ms) over 5m by model
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) * 1000

# p99 latency (ms) global
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) * 1000

# tokens/sec per host
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (instance)
```

Nina: If you want TTFT specifically, use the ttft metric we emit: `time_to_first_token_ms` (summary). Example: 
``
# p99 TTFT for model=redwood-4x
quantile_over_time(0.99, rate(time_to_first_token_ms{model="redwood-4x"}[5m]))
```
Group by `route` or `model` to find hotspots. Also check the KV-cache hit panel — cold cache can massively bump TTFT.

Jordan: Thanks — curious about alert tuning. Current alert `HighRequestP99` fires when p99 > 500ms for 3m. That ended up noisy last night. Suggestions?

Priya: Two options: raise threshold OR make it conditional on tokens/sec (so we only alert on sustained latency under load). Example composite rule idea: alert when p99 > 700ms AND tokens/sec > X (to avoid noise from single long generative calls).

Mike: Agree. Another pattern: use burn-rate style for short bursts + sustained rule for longer windows. E.g. p99>700ms for 5m OR p99>1000ms for 1m. Also consider scoping by `model` and `route` to avoid global noise. :+1:

Nina: If you want to detect queuing, look for high server-side latency + decreasing tokens/sec per instance. PromQL approx: 
```
# detect potential queuing: high p95 + tokens/sec drop (5m window)
(p95_query > 700) and (sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[5m])) by (instance) < threshold)
```
We can tune threshold per fleet size.

Samir: I opened an alert PR with a per-model threshold approach and a docs section on how to pick thresholds: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/421 — PTAL @Priya @Nina.

Priya: If you want a quick panel snapshot, hit Export -> share panel link and paste here. I can attach to the PR and mark as non-blocking.

Mike: FYI, I left a short code-review comment on the PR about adding a runbook reference for on-call.

Jordan: Thanks. One quick thing — where do we store the canonical mapping of dashboard panels to alert rules? I couldn't find a single mapping last time.

Nina: We're keeping a mapping file in the repo: observability/dashboards/alerts_map.md — link in the PR description should point to it. If it's missing any new panels, add them to the PR.

Jordan: Great. I'll collect the screenshots and trace links and reply in the PR. If we decide to change the alert, I prefer the tokens/sec gating approach.

Priya: Sounds good. Ping me after you paste the panel links and I'll approve quick tweaks if it's low risk. :rocket:

Jordan: Appreciate it — will update before EOD.
